'''''Veronica scutellata''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Plantaginaceae|plantain family]] known by the common names '''marsh speedwell''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''skullcap speedwell''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=VESC2|taxon=Veronica scutellata|access-date=2019-03-05}}</ref> and '''grassleaf speedwell'''. It is native to [[temperate climate|temperate]] Asia, Europe, northern Africa, and northern North America <ref name = GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref> in a variety of wet habitats.

==Description==
It is a [[herbaceous]] (non-woody) [[perennial plant|perennial]] [[Veronica (plant)|speedwell]] that produces a creeping stem that roots at its nodes then ascends to flower, to {{convert|60|cm|in|abbr=on}} in length, using other vegetation as a scaffold. The paired leaves alternate in direction and are very narrow and pointed, stalkless, somewhat rigid, often with a yellowed or reddened hue, with obscure teeth (or none), and curling under at the edges; it initially rises with its leaves vertical to push through vegetation and later opens them sideways to anchor its position.<ref name="farmanagh"/> The alternating floral spikes emerge from the stem with the base of the leaf stalks, each a sparse array of several flowers, the flowers themselves on long thin stalks. The flowers are small ({{convert|3-7|mm|in|abbr=on}} diam), pale lilac, pale blue or whitish, although sometimes strongly coloured, with accentuated veins, which at maturity form flat capsules 3–5 mm long, deeply divided at the top. Although typically lacking in much hair (var. scutella), some forms are densely hairy usually with a mixture of glandular and non-glandular hairs, especially in drier habitats (var. villosa).

==Taxonomy==
''Veronica scutellata'' was given its scientific name in 1753 by [[Carl Linnaeus]]. It is part of the genus [[Veronica (plant)|''Veronica'']], which is classified in the [[Plantaginaceae]] family. The species has no accepted [[Variety (botany)|varieties]], but 11 have been described that are among its 23 [[Synonym (botany)|synonyms]] including {{table row counter|id=Synonyms}} species.<ref name="POWO">{{cite POWO |id=812639-1 |title=''Veronica scutellata'' L. |access-date=30 April 2026}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==

It is native to Europe (but rare near the Mediterranean <ref name="FEU">{{cite book |title=Flora Europaea, vol. 3, p. 247 |author=Tutin}}</ref>), North Asia, Most of North America and Algeria, and is not indicated as introduced to any country.<ref name="POWO" />

Its habitat is marshes, shores, water banks and a wide range of other wet places, particularly acidic. In America its altitude range is 0–1800(2400) m,<ref name="FNA"/> in Turkey it is found along the north at 0–500 m.<ref name="FoT">{{cite book |title=Flora of Turkey and the East Aegean Islands, vol. 6, p. 753 |author=Davis}}</ref>
